  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The workflow still bootstraps `verify_integration_fingerprints.py` and `review_conflict_resolve.sh` from the branch checkout first because the main-first `MAIN_PRIMARY_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS` path is absent.

- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:451,666/1190 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The main-primary bootstrap loop that should deliver the new verifier/resolver from main is not implemented in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`.
  WHY: Without main-first bootstrap logic, the resolver keeps using the old branch copy and the new delta-verification behavior never activates on stuck branches.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:878,1198-1200 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `capture_baseline_state()` does not receive the parsed `ref`, so `--baseline-fingerprints-state --ref <git_ref>` captures the working tree instead of the requested ref.
  WHY: Compare mode later honors the ref, so the baseline and comparison trees can diverge and produce false regressions or missed regressions.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:~123-134,~886,~1038 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Fingerprint paths are normalized in a way that still lets absolute or out-of-root paths flow into `open()` and `git show`.
  WHY: A malformed or malicious fingerprint JSON can trigger reads outside the checkout, creating an information-disclosure and path-traversal risk.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:568-575 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The invalid-regex compile warning is printed to stdout instead of stderr.
  WHY: `--list-violated-files` expects file paths only on stdout, so the warning contaminates machine-readable output and downstream consumers can treat it as a phantom path.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:967-974 | severity=medium | confidence=4

  PROBLEM: `PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1` markers interpolate raw `path` and `regex` values without escaping double quotes.
  WHY: A quote in either field breaks marker field boundaries and makes the drift-audit line unparsable.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:150,190,206-212,265-274 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]

  WHY: A mistyped `INTEGRATION_VERIFY_REF` or invalid git state can fail open and make verification pass when it should surface a plumbing error.

  WHY: The baseline JSON ends up with `head_sha` metadata that does not match the tree whose fingerprint state was recorded.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py: lines 1198-1200 (`return capture_baseline_state(data, baseline_out_path, branch)`) and line 878 (`def capture_baseline_state(fingerprints, out_path, branch)`) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `capture_baseline_state()` does not accept or forward the `ref` parameter.
  WHY: `--baseline-fingerprints-state --ref <git_ref>` captures the working-tree state while compare mode later uses the supplied ref, so delta comparisons are against the wrong tree.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py: lines 967-974 (`_emit_pre_existing_drift_marker`) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1` markers interpolate raw `path` and `regex` values inside double-quoted fields without escaping.
  WHY: A fingerprint regex containing `"` produces an ambiguous marker and the planned drift-audit parser cannot reliably split the fields.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py: lines 206-212 (ref-mode `_read_file_result` except handler) and lines 265-274 (ref-mode `_path_exists_result` except handler) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Both ref-mode `subprocess.run` calls use bare `except Exception` and map all failures to the same result as an absent file.
  WHY: A mistyped `INTEGRATION_VERIFY_REF` or non-git checkout can silently pass verification instead of surfacing the plumbing failure, although the reviewer notes this is a deliberate fail-open tradeoff.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: lines 959-978 (OPTIONAL_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS and bootstrap loops) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The workflow bootstraps `verify_integration_fingerprints.py` via branch-first ordering and does not have the required main-first loop.
  WHY: Old branch copies remain installed on stuck integration branches, so the self-heal code shipped to `main` never reaches the branches it is meant to fix.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py: lines 572-575 (`_evaluate_fp_state`, regex compile failure path) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The invalid-regex warning is printed to stdout instead of stderr.
  WHY: `--list-violated-files` output is supposed to be file paths only, so the warning contaminates the machine-readable stream and downstream consumers can treat it as a path.
- docs/completed/integration-sync-resolver-self-heal-plan.md: line 625 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The relative link `./orchestrator-validation-resilience-plan.md` resolves to `docs/completed/orchestrator-validation-resilience-plan.md`, which does not exist.
  WHY: Documentation consumers following the cross-reference hit a nonexistent target.
- docs/plans/integration-sync-resolver-self-heal-plan.md: line 626 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The relative link `./judge-loop-and-reissue-plan.md` resolves to `docs/plans/judge-loop-and-reissue-plan.md`, which does not exist.
  WHY: The referenced file was moved to `docs/completed/judge-loop-and-reissue-plan.md`, so the link is broken.
